power_model_for_speed_credit.rule: Share of crashes after = (V_after / V_before) ^ exponent, on mean speed, for a fix that changes mean speed and nothing else about the street.
power_model_for_speed_credit.basis: Trafikverket 2026 Table 42 (tätort column): TØI 1034/2009 exponents levelled to Elvik et al. 2019, which gives 5.5 for killed and 3.9 for seriously injured across all roads; Elvik et al. 2019 exponential model coefficients 0.08 (killed), 0.06 (serious), 0.04 (slight) per km/h.
power_model_for_speed_credit.older_urban_values: Elvik 2009 urban and residential: injury crashes 1.2 (0.7 to 1.7), injured people 1.4 (0.4 to 2.4), serious injuries 2.0 (0.8 to 3.2), deaths 3.0 (-0.5 to 6.5), from Frith and Tate Table 4 [secondary — read 2026-11-25]. Cameron and Elvik 2010: about 1.6 for death and serious injury on urban arterials [secondary — verify, per repo note].
power_model_for_speed_credit.worked_example: A mean speed cut from 25 to 22 mph gives (22/25)^2.6 = 0.72, so about 28% fewer seriously injured people, and (22/25)^1.4 = 0.84, 16% fewer slightly injured [inference — mine].
power_model_for_speed_credit.how_much_mean_speed_moves: Signs alone: Norway found mean speed falls about 2.5 km/h for a 10 km/h limit cut and 7.5 km/h for 20 km/h (Danish Effekthåndbog 5.4) [primary — read 2026-11-25]; SF's nine corridors showed no change in median speed (SFMTA 2024, per repo note). Humps: 40.8 to 28.0 km/h (Danish 4.5). Feedback signs: about 5 km/h (Danish 4.3). Cameras: SF reports the share 10+ mph over (-84%), not mean speed, so SF's cameras can't be credited through the power model until mean speeds are published.
power_model_for_speed_credit.caveats: Apply only to the crashes on the streets whose speed changed. Our SF cross-section could not estimate a speed exponent (-1.6 to +3.4) because residential speeds span only 20 to 29 mph (2026-11-18 note). Elvik et al. 2019's own urban table is unretrieved; the Trafikverket levelling is the read we have.

gaps: Hit Object (914 hurt, 130 KSI) and Overturned (438, 43) are crash types from grouping_alternatives, not size_families families; results.json has no cross-tab of crash type by violation, by night or by what object was hit, so loss-of-control fixes can't be given a target share.
Rear End as a crash type (4,583 hurt, 107 KSI) is three times following too closely (1,398, 20); the overlap with unsafe speed and other violations is not in results.json.

Bicycle-involved unsafe speed (581, 94 KSI): 554 of those hurt are bicyclists, but the at-fault party (driver or bicyclist) is not split, so driver-speed fixes may reach only part of it; fixes for bicyclist speed (downhill design, e-bike speed rules) have no source in this lane.
No mean-speed figure for SF's cameras, so they can't be credited through the power model; SFMTA publishes only the share 10+ mph over.
Elvik et al. 2019 full text (urban exponents with intervals) unretrieved: the brage.unit.no host failed and core.ac.uk returned 403. The Trafikverket levelled table stands in.
TØI handbook online (tshandbok.no) not reachable this session: chapters on speed limits, police enforcement, ISA and section control were taken from repo notes or not at all.
Leeds ISA Implementation Scenarios report: certificate expired, not opened; ISA crash estimates are from a search summary.

No SF cost found for: a plain four-to-three restripe, radar feedback signs, signal retiming per intersection, high-friction surfacing, lighting upgrades, fixed-object removal, mobile camera units, AEB or ISA in City purchases.
City fleet and ride-hail share of SF crashes is unknown (needed to size ISA and AEB fleet rules); the parties table carries vehicle type but not ownership.
Night-time 'rest in red' signal operation for late-night speeders (the one vehicle-only cell that passed the severity test: 664 hurt, 80 KSI) has no source in this lane.
No study of upgrading street lighting on already-lit city streets was opened; the Danish figure is for newly lit roads.
Paris 30 km/h, Spain's 2021 30 km/h urban default and Pontevedra: no crash evaluation opened this session.
Motorcycle ABS and motorcyclist share of the vehicles-only speed and loss-of-control groups not checked.

Red-light cameras raise rear-end crashes (FHWA-HRT-05-049: side-impact -25%, rear-end +15%; Danish 5.7: injuries -15% but crashes only -2%); that harm to the following-too-closely group belongs on the red-light lane's records.

bicycle involved | following too closely (80 hurt, 6 KSI) and pedestrian involved | following too closely (13, 1) get no fix record: Cicchino 2017 measures car-to-car rear-end crashes only, and no source opened gives a rear-end effect for drivers striking bicyclists; lower speeds and separated bike lanes (other lanes) are the candidates.
DUI is a large share of late-night loss-of-control in most cities; it is the DUI lane's, and the overlap with unsafe speed is not in results.json.
